item: Land Belton, Seguin, and Cibolo's researched setback tables using gate.ts's new primary-source-verified state (#628).
checkpoint: DONE. legacy-design-tools PR #629 merged to main (4d340524), branch deleted.
whatShipped: Registered belton-tx.json (22 codified base districts), seguin-tx.json (11 districts), cibolo-tx.json (4 SF districts) in lib/adapters/src/local/setbacks/index.ts. Updated the three cities' zoning-layers.ts comments from 'SETBACK TABLE OWED' to reflect delivery. Only Waco and Killeen now carry the OWED marker (Waco: Engine's hauska-engine PR #393 relabeled its own copy; Killeen is this lane's next task, see below).
realDefectFoundAndFixedBeforeLanding: The three delivered research files predated gate.ts's primary-source-verified state and used human-verified/asserted with fabricated atom_did values styled to look like real corpus citations (e.g. cibolo_tx/udc/art14.1-14.2/sf1) -- landing them as-is would have reproduced Belton's original 254-G2-block problem across all three cities, since neither asserted nor human-verified skips the atom-resolution check (only primary-source-verified does). Live-verified belton_tx/seguin_tx/cibolo_tx are genuinely zero in the real code-section atoms store (confirming primary-source-verified is the correct state, not a shortcut) before relabeling every provenance entry and stripping every atom_did. Wrote a real test (beltonSeguinCiboloSetbacks.test.ts) that runs the actual runSetbackGate against each table with an empty atom corpus and asserts zero blocks -- not just that the JSON parses -- so this is now a permanent regression check, not a one-time manual verification.
researchQualityConfirmed: Reviewed the substantive research before landing rather than treating the hand-off as a rubber stamp. Belton's O-2 side-yard clause is a genuine internal ordinance-text ambiguity between a 'None (interior)' reading and a '25 ft adjacent side property lines' reading -- already coded at reduced confidence (0.55) with the ambiguity disclosed in the quote rather than silently resolved either way; also correctly disambiguated Belton, TX from a same-named Belton, Missouri whose planning pages surface first in generic web search. Cibolo's SF-5/SF-6 are live GIS zoning codes (confirmed via the city's own ArcGIS FeatureServer) with no dimensional-standards subsection anywhere in the current 438-page UDC -- cross-checked against a second, independent PDF extraction (PyMuPDF page-image read vs. pdftotext) to rule out an OCR artifact, and against the city's prior 2023-08 UDC to confirm the gap predates this research pass -- honestly omitted from districts[] rather than interpolated from a neighboring district's numbers. Both handled exactly per this codebase's established honest-gap conventions.
testing: New beltonSeguinCiboloSetbacks.test.ts (8 tests: routing + district-count for all three, real gate execution with zero blocks for all three, Belton O-2 confidence/disclosure assertion, Cibolo SF-5/SF-6 omission assertion). Full lib/adapters suite: 399 passing. lib/cad-ingest unaffected: 288 passing. tsc --build clean. CI green (Test job 11m35s).
openFollowUp: Killeen's citation-resolution against its real 637-atom corpus is still open -- this lane is picking it up next. Per cente-67's Round Rock finding, atom count alone does not guarantee the specific cited numbers survived ingestion as round-trippable bodyText; per-section content needs the same live check before choosing between real atom-backed citations and primary-source-verified for Killeen.
